results.title: TraffiTech-GH goes live as MTTD rolls out camera-based speeding checks
results.content: The Motor Traffic and Transport Department (MTTD) says it is ready to roll out its TraffiTech-GH digital traffic enforcement system on Sunday, November 1, 2026, with cameras expected to detect speeding offences and electronic notices sent to vehicle owners. The department’s Director of Education, Research and Training, ACP Alexander Kwaku Obeng, said preparations had been completed for the launch, which will initially target speeding at locations identified as prone to road crashes. “Tomorrow, 1st November, we are set, everything is ready, and we are taking off,” he said. Under the system, cameras mounted in police vehicles and on tripods will capture vehicles exceeding prescribed speed limits. The MTTD will process the footage and send electronic violation notices to the phone numbers of vehicle owners registered with the department.

results.title: Government raises daily feeding allowance for prison inmates from GH¢1.80 to GH¢5
results.content: The government has increased the daily feeding allowance for Ghana Prisons Service inmates from GH¢1.80 to GH¢5, Vice President Professor Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang announced. She said the increase forms part of broader efforts to improve conditions in the country's prisons, strengthen rehabilitation programmes and enhance the operational capacity of the Prisons Service. The Vice President announced this at the commissioning of Cadet Course Intakes 33, 34 and 35 into the Senior Officer Corps of the Ghana Prisons Service at Adansi Fumso in the Ashanti Region. She said improving conditions in prisons must remain a priority, stressing that the work of the Prisons Service extends beyond keeping offenders in custody to protecting the public, respecting human dignity and preparing inmates for reintegration into society.

results.title: Is the NPP orchestrating an undemocratic power grab to shield incumbent MPs ahead of 2028?
results.content: The New Patriotic Party (NPP), historically revered as a bastion of intra-party democracy and constitutional governance in Ghana, appears to be executing a retrograde maneuver. As the party prepares to select its parliamentary standard-bearers for the crucial 2028 General Elections, its leadership seems intent on compromising the very values and foundational tenets that once defined its identity. Rather than adhering to the time-tested, egalitarian tradition of opening nominations to all qualified aspirants, the party leadership, via recent official circulars and a press conference convened by the General Secretary, is introducing a dubious, unprecedented political experiment. While dynamic change and innovation are vital features of organizational growth, novel mechanisms must be approached with utmost prudence.

results.title: 2026 Luv FM-Republic Bank Habitat mini-clinic records huge success in Kumasi
results.content: The 2026 Luv FM-Republic Bank Habitat Fair has begun with a mini-clinic in Kumasi, bringing together players in Ghana’s housing and construction industry to promote affordable and accessible homeownership. The event, held on October 29, 2026, at the Opoku Trading Arena in Adum, offered prospective homeowners, property developers and industry professionals an opportunity to engage institutions providing housing services, construction materials, financing and interior decoration solutions. Now in its eighth year, the Habitat Fair seeks to address some of the challenges associated with land acquisition, building and homeownership, particularly in the Ashanti Region.

results.title: From stability to transformation: 5 tests for Ghana’s 2027 Budget
results.content: The government proposes lowering the primary surplus on a commitment basis from 1.5% to 0.5% of GDP from 2027. A primary surplus is the excess of revenue over spending before interest payments. Reducing it leaves more room for expenditure, but also means a smaller contribution towards containing debt, other things being equal.
